title: Isaiah Chapter 49 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Isaiah chapter 49 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Isaiah Chapter 49 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Isaiah Chapter 49.

questions.question: In Isaiah 49, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: The LORD hath called me from the womb
I will also give thee for a light to the Gentiles
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD hath called me from the womb
questions.explanation: This phrase appears first in Isaiah 49:1, which is the earliest verse in the provided text.

questions.question: Who hath called the speaker from the womb according to Isaiah 49?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 49:1 states, 'The LORD hath called me from the womb.'

questions.question: According to Isaiah 49, how is the speaker's mouth described?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 49:2 says, 'And he hath made my mouth like a sharp sword.'

questions.question: What has the LORD made the speaker to be, as stated in Isaiah 49?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 49:3 says, 'Thou art my servant, O Israel.'

questions.question: What did the speaker say about his labor in Isaiah 49?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 49:4 states, 'Then I said, I have laboured in vain.'

questions.question: Who formed the speaker from the womb as per Isaiah 49?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 49:5 says, 'saith the LORD that formed me from the womb.'

questions.question: What is the speaker to bring again to the LORD according to Isaiah 49?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 49:5 states, 'to bring Jacob again to him.'

questions.question: In Isaiah 49, what additional role is given to the servant besides raising up the tribes of Jacob?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 49:6 says, 'I will also give thee for a light to the Gentiles.'

questions.question: According to Isaiah 49, who shall see and arise because of the LORD?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 49:7 states, 'Kings shall see and arise.'

questions.question: What has the LORD said about the time He has heard and helped the speaker, according to Isaiah 49?
options: In an acceptable time and a day of salvation
In the days of darkness and despair
In the time of judgment and wrath
In the hour of weakness and fear
questions.correctAnswer: In an acceptable time and a day of salvation
questions.explanation: Isaiah 49:8 says, 'In an acceptable time have I heard thee, and in a day of salvation have I helped thee.'

questions.question: According to Isaiah 49, what are the prisoners told to do?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 49:9 says, 'That thou mayest say to the prisoners, Go forth.'

questions.question: Isaiah 49 says the LORD called the speaker from his mother's womb. True or False?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 49:1 states, 'The LORD hath called me from the womb; from the bowels of my mother hath he made mention of my name.'

questions.question: According to Isaiah 49, the LORD promises to preserve the speaker and give him for a covenant of the people. True or False?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 49:8 says, 'I will preserve thee, and give thee for a covenant of the people.'

questions.question: Isaiah 49 says that the speaker will become king over all the nations. True or False?
questions.explanation: The text does not say the speaker will become king over all nations; instead, it says kings shall see and arise and princes shall worship (Isaiah 49:7), but not that the speaker becomes king.

questions.question: Isaiah 49 states that the speaker will restore the desolate heritages and establish the earth to inherit them. True or False?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 49:8 says the LORD will cause to inherit the desolate heritages and establish the earth, but it does not say the speaker will do this himself.

medium.title: Isaiah Chapter 49 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Isaiah Chapter 49 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What will happen to those who are led by the one who has mercy on them, according to Isaiah 49:10?
options: They shall not hunger nor thirst
They shall not see the light
questions.correctAnswer: They shall not hunger nor thirst
questions.explanation: This is correct as it is stated in Isaiah 49:10, which assures comfort and provision for those led by Him.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 49:11 promise will happen if someone follows God's ways as stated in that verse?
options: Mountains will be made a way
They shall suffer heat and thirst
questions.correctAnswer: Mountains will be made a way
questions.explanation: Isaiah 49:11 indicates that God will make a way through the mountains, symbolizing His guidance and provision.

questions.question: From which directions will people come, according to Isaiah 49:12?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 49:12 specifies that people will come from the north and from the west, indicating a gathering from far places.

questions.question: What is the reaction of the heavens and earth in Isaiah 49:13?
options: They will be joyful and sing
questions.correctAnswer: They will be joyful and sing
questions.explanation: Isaiah 49:13 describes a call for heavens and earth to sing and be joyful because of God's comfort to His people.

questions.question: What does Zion express in Isaiah 49:14?
questions.explanation: In Isaiah 49:14, Zion expresses a feeling of abandonment, stating that the LORD has forsaken her.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 49:15, can a woman forget her child?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 49:15 acknowledges that while a woman may forget her child, God will not forget His people.

questions.question: What promise does God make about His people in Isaiah 49:16?
options: He has graven them on His hands
questions.correctAnswer: He has graven them on His hands
questions.explanation: Isaiah 49:16 states that God has engraved His people on the palms of His hands, signifying His constant remembrance and care.

questions.question: What will happen to the children of Zion according to Isaiah 49:17?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 49:17 states that Zion's children shall make haste, indicating a return or gathering of God’s people.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 49:18, what is the imagery used to describe how Zion will be clothed?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 49:18 uses the imagery of being clothed as with an ornament, signifying beauty and honor in the gathering of His people.

questions.question: How does Isaiah 49:4 reflect on the servant's feelings about his labor?
options: He feels it was in vain
questions.correctAnswer: He feels it was in vain
questions.explanation: Isaiah 49:4 reveals the servant's feelings of having labored in vain, yet he finds hope in the LORD's judgment.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 49:6 indicate about the servant's role to the Gentiles?
options: To be a light to the Gentiles
questions.correctAnswer: To be a light to the Gentiles
questions.explanation: Isaiah 49:6 states that the servant is to be a light to the Gentiles, indicating a mission of salvation and guidance.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 49:7 say about the one whom the nations despise?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 49:7 assures that despite being despised, kings will recognize and honor the servant because of the LORD's faithfulness.

questions.question: Is it true that God has forgotten His people, according to Isaiah 49:15?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 49:15 clarifies that even if a woman may forget her child, God will not forget His people.

questions.question: Is it true that the mountains will be made a way, as promised in Isaiah 49:11?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 49:11 promises that God will make the mountains a way, symbolizing His guidance for His people.

questions.question: Is it true that Zion will be clothed as with dust, according to Isaiah 49:18?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 49:18 states that Zion will be clothed as with an ornament, not with dust, indicating beauty and honor.

hard.title: Isaiah Chapter 49 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Isaiah Chapter 49.

questions.question: What will happen to the desolate places according to Isaiah 49:19?
options: They shall be too narrow by reason of the inhabitants.
questions.correctAnswer: They shall be too narrow by reason of the inhabitants.
questions.explanation: This answer is correct because Isaiah 49:19 states that the waste and desolate places shall be too narrow due to the increase of inhabitants.

questions.question: What do the children say in Isaiah 49:20?
options: We have plenty of space here.
The place is too strait for me: give place to me that I may dwell.
We are happy with our situation.
We do not want to move.
questions.correctAnswer: The place is too strait for me: give place to me that I may dwell.
questions.explanation: Isaiah 49:20 records that the children, after experiencing loss, express that the place is too narrow for them, seeking more space.

questions.question: What does the speaker wonder about in Isaiah 49:21?
questions.explanation: In Isaiah 49:21, the speaker reflects on the new children they have received despite previously losing their own, questioning who brought them forth.

questions.question: What does the Lord promise in Isaiah 49:25 regarding the captives?
options: Even the captives of the mighty shall be taken away.
questions.correctAnswer: Even the captives of the mighty shall be taken away.
questions.explanation: Isaiah 49:25 indicates God's promise that He will deliver the captives of the mighty, asserting His power to save.

questions.question: Who does the Lord say will carry the sons and daughters according to Isaiah 49:22?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 49:22 states that kings will carry the sons and queens will carry the daughters, indicating a reversal of roles in honor and care.

questions.question: What will happen to those who oppress according to Isaiah 49:26?
options: They shall be drunk with their own blood.
questions.correctAnswer: They shall be drunk with their own blood.
questions.explanation: Isaiah 49:26 foretells that those who oppress will suffer consequences, described vividly as being drunk with their own blood.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word 'nâṭâh' in Isaiah 49:22 mean?
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word 'nâṭâh' means 'to stretch out,' relating to God's promise to extend His hand to the Gentiles in Isaiah 49:22.

questions.question: What literary device is used in Isaiah 49:23 when describing kings and queens?
questions.explanation: The description of kings and queens as nursing fathers and mothers in Isaiah 49:23 is a metaphor illustrating their role in nurturing and caring for Israel.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage connects to the theme of restoration in Isaiah 49:19?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 36:26-27 speaks about God restoring His people and giving them a new heart and spirit, connecting to the theme of restoration in Isaiah 49:19.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage connects to the promise of deliverance in Isaiah 49:25?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 61:1 speaks of proclaiming liberty to the captives, echoing the promise of deliverance found in Isaiah 49:25.

questions.question: What comes before Isaiah 49:19?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 49:18 discusses Zion's longing and lament, which is the context preceding the promise in Isaiah 49:19.

questions.question: What comes after Isaiah 49:26?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 49:26 concludes with a declaration of God's power, leading into the promise of restoration and new beginnings.

questions.question: The theme of God's salvation in Isaiah 49 can be connected to which New Testament concept?
questions.explanation: The Great Commission relates to the theme of salvation and reaching out to all nations, echoing Isaiah 49's message of being a light to the Gentiles.

questions.question: God's promise that He will not forget His people, as stated in Isaiah 49:15, is true.
questions.explanation: This statement is true as Isaiah 49:15 emphasizes God's unwavering commitment to His people, assuring that He will not forget them.

questions.question: The imagery of nursing mothers in Isaiah 49:23 implies weakness and vulnerability.
questions.explanation: This statement is false; the imagery of nursing mothers in Isaiah 49:23 symbolizes strength and care, highlighting the honor given to Israel by powerful figures.

theological.title: Isaiah Chapter 49 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Isaiah Chapter 49 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Isaiah 49:3 teach about God's relationship to Israel?
options: Israel is God's servant in whom He will be glorified
Israel is abandoned due to sin
Israel is equal to other nations
Israel earns God's favor through works
questions.correctAnswer: Israel is God's servant in whom He will be glorified
questions.explanation: Isaiah 49:3 explicitly states, 'Thou art my servant, O Israel, in whom I will be glorified,' teaching the doctrine of Israel as God's chosen servant for His glory.

questions.question: What doctrine concerning divine election and calling is taught in Isaiah 49:1?
options: God calls His servant from the womb, indicating predestination
God calls only the mature and righteous
God's calling is based on human merit
questions.correctAnswer: God calls His servant from the womb, indicating predestination
questions.explanation: Isaiah 49:1 says, 'The LORD hath called me from the womb,' indicating divine election and calling before birth, which supports the doctrine of predestination.

questions.question: What doctrine about salvation does Isaiah 49:6 teach regarding the scope of God's redemptive plan?
options: God's salvation extends to the Gentiles to the ends of the earth
Salvation is limited to Israel only
Salvation is earned by obedience alone
questions.correctAnswer: God's salvation extends to the Gentiles to the ends of the earth
questions.explanation: Isaiah 49:6 declares that the servant will be 'a light to the Gentiles' and 'my salvation unto the end of the earth,' teaching the doctrine of universal scope of salvation.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Isaiah 49:15 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 49:15 compares God's compassion to a mother's, emphasizing that God will not forget His people, demonstrating His mercy.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is primarily shown in Isaiah 49:16 when God says He has graven His people upon the palms of His hands?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 49:16 illustrates God's unbreakable commitment to His people by saying He has inscribed them on His hands, symbolizing covenant faithfulness.

questions.question: How does Isaiah 49:8 connect to the New Testament theme of the 'acceptable time' and 'day of salvation'?
options: It anticipates Christ's ministry offering salvation at the appointed time
It refers only to Israel's political restoration
It describes a past event with no future fulfillment
It limits salvation to temple rituals
questions.correctAnswer: It anticipates Christ's ministry offering salvation at the appointed time
questions.explanation: Isaiah 49:8 speaks of God hearing in an 'acceptable time' and helping in a 'day of salvation,' which the NT applies to Christ's redemptive work (2 Corinthians 6:2).

questions.question: What redemptive-historical theme does Isaiah 49:22 develop regarding Gentile inclusion?
options: God lifting His hand to the Gentiles to bring in His people prefigures the inclusion of Gentiles in the church
The Gentiles will remain outsiders forever
The Gentiles must be conquered militarily
The Gentiles are irrelevant to God's plan
questions.correctAnswer: God lifting His hand to the Gentiles to bring in His people prefigures the inclusion of Gentiles in the church
questions.explanation: Isaiah 49:22 describes God raising a standard to the Gentiles who will carry Israel’s children, symbolizing Gentile inclusion in salvation history fulfilled in the church.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Isaiah 49:14 and Isaiah 49:15 teach about God's faithfulness despite human despair?
options: Though Zion feels forsaken, God will never forget His people
God abandons His people when they despair
Human feelings are proof of divine rejection
God’s faithfulness depends on human perception
questions.correctAnswer: Though Zion feels forsaken, God will never forget His people
questions.explanation: Isaiah 49:14 expresses Zion’s feeling of abandonment, but 49:15 assures that God’s compassion and remembrance are unfailing despite human feelings.

questions.question: What combined teaching about divine protection and restoration is found in Isaiah 49:25-26 and Isaiah 49:17?
options: God will contend for His people and cause their enemies to be defeated and removed
God allows enemies to triumph permanently
Restoration depends on Israel’s military strength
Divine protection is uncertain and conditional
questions.correctAnswer: God will contend for His people and cause their enemies to be defeated and removed
questions.explanation: Isaiah 49:25-26 promises God’s intervention against oppressors, while 49:17 speaks of destroyers leaving, affirming divine protection and restoration.

questions.question: What doctrine emerges from synthesizing Isaiah 49:9 and Isaiah 49:10 about God's provision for the redeemed?
options: God provides spiritual and physical nourishment and guidance to His people
God leaves the redeemed to fend for themselves
Provision is solely material without spiritual care
The redeemed will continue to experience hunger and thirst
questions.correctAnswer: God provides spiritual and physical nourishment and guidance to His people
questions.explanation: Isaiah 49:9-10 describes God’s care freeing prisoners and leading them by springs of water, teaching comprehensive provision and guidance.

questions.question: Skeptics claim Isaiah 49:4 shows that the servant’s labor is pointless and God’s promises are empty. What does the passage actually teach?
options: Though the servant feels his labor is in vain, his judgment and work are with the LORD, affirming divine purpose
The servant’s labor is truly vain and without meaning
God abandons the servant due to failure
The servant’s work is irrelevant to salvation
questions.correctAnswer: Though the servant feels his labor is in vain, his judgment and work are with the LORD, affirming divine purpose
questions.explanation: Isaiah 49:4 acknowledges the servant’s discouragement but affirms that his work and judgment belong to God, emphasizing divine purpose despite human feelings.

questions.question: What doctrine does Isaiah 49:12 teach about the gathering of God’s people in the eschatological age?
options: God’s people will be gathered from all directions, including distant lands, symbolizing universal restoration
God’s people will remain scattered without hope
Gathering is limited to local regions
Only Israel proper will be gathered, excluding others
questions.correctAnswer: God’s people will be gathered from all directions, including distant lands, symbolizing universal restoration
questions.explanation: Isaiah 49:12 mentions people coming from far, north, west, and Sinim, indicating a universal ingathering in the eschatological restoration.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is most clearly demonstrated in Isaiah 49:8 concerning the 'acceptable time' and 'day of salvation'?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 49:8 emphasizes God’s sovereign timing in hearing and helping the servant at the appointed 'acceptable time' and 'day of salvation.'

questions.question: What theological insight does Isaiah 49:23 provide concerning the relationship between Israel and Gentile rulers?
options: Kings and queens will serve as nursing parents to Israel, indicating Gentile submission and blessing
Gentile rulers will oppress Israel permanently
Israel and Gentiles remain separate with no interaction
questions.correctAnswer: Kings and queens will serve as nursing parents to Israel, indicating Gentile submission and blessing
questions.explanation: Isaiah 49:23 depicts Gentile monarchs humbling themselves to nurture Israel, symbolizing Gentile inclusion and honor toward God’s people.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Isaiah 49:18 and Isaiah 49:20 teach about God's restoration of Israel's population after exile?
options: God will multiply Israel’s descendants abundantly after loss and desolation
Israel will remain desolate and barren
Restoration is only spiritual, not numerical
questions.correctAnswer: God will multiply Israel’s descendants abundantly after loss and desolation
questions.explanation: Isaiah 49:18-20 promises Israel will be clothed with those gathered and that the place will become too narrow for the increased inhabitants, teaching restoration and multiplication.
